title: the 6-3-2 system, *stress-tested*
dek: [VERIFIED] A live, read-only audit of Jen's Instagram-to-conversation path, a twelve-journey diagnostic stress test, and the strongest source-bounded proof currently available for ICPs 6, 3, and 2.
sources: Instagram, Linktree, buyer tools, 2,779 archived captions, system files

sections.heading: the *verdict*
sections.body:
Jen has useful buyer content, a live Linktree, search and calculator utilities, and locally drafted reply and measurement logic. She does not yet have a verified end-to-end conversion system that carries a buyer from a post into a qualified, attributable conversation.

The 6-3-2 diagnostic is strategically sound but not build-ready in its original form. The three ICPs overlap, so routing must be based on today's blocker, not a forced identity choice.

The archive also does not support three equally strong 6-3-2 client stories: #6 is a strong provisional proof, #3 is a provisional fit needing confirmation, and #2 has empathy evidence but no client transaction proof.

items.label: DIAGNOSTIC STRESS TESTS
items.note: Selected ICPs, overlaps, nurture, representation, geography, privacy, fair housing, and professional scope.
Both available stories are provisional; #2 has no client case.

rows.claim: The live profile opens a conversation but does not name a concrete next object.
rows.evidence: The bio promises seamless, stress-free buying and selling. A pinned first-time-buyer Reel says Jen's DMs are open; another recent buyer Reel invites a message for real numbers and honest answers. Neither identifies a diagnostic, result, saved resource, or consultation path.

rows.claim: The Linktree is a mixed menu, not a 6-3-2 buyer journey.
rows.evidence: The first button is an unrelated music/ecommerce store. Buyer tools appear below it alongside a podcast, blog, team site, and playlist. There is no First Home Valley diagnostic, consultation link, or visible 6-3-2 route. The most recent internal Insights audit recorded 12 external-link taps from 1,589 profile visits, or 0.76%; that shows movement, not qualified-buyer conversion.

rows.claim: The MLS and calculator links are utilities, not a verified qualification layer.
rows.evidence: The MLS page offers property-search app access. The affordability and mortgage calculators request scenario inputs and display assumptions, but expose no visible route-specific question, contact capture, or continuity into Jen's conversation. Any downstream CRM linkage remains unconfirmed because no forms were submitted.

rows.claim: Existing local files contain reply and attribution designs, not operating proof.
rows.evidence: Four saved replies exist locally; installation and use are unconfirmed. The lead-path audit defines qualified DM, consultation, signed-client, and closing stages, but current outcomes are unattributed. Funnel rates remain placeholders.

rows.claim: The live positioning and current system canon disagree.
rows.evidence: The approved direction uses First Home Valley with ICPs 6, 3, and 2. BRAND.yaml still points to ENGINE-V2 as canon; ENGINE-V2 says the niche is the place, not the person, and BRAND.yaml bans the phrase 'your first home.' Downstream production could silently revert unless this authority order is reconciled.

sections.heading: the diagnostic passes *conditionally*
sections.body:
Clean examples passed: two W-2 buyers aligning payment and commutes; a solo buyer needing decision support; and a mixed W-2/1099 buyer organizing a lender-ready question.

Overlap examples exposed the flaw: siblings co-buying with variable income and a newly self-employed buyer purchasing with a W-2 partner both belong to #6 and #2. A single-choice identity branch loses material context.

Non-fit examples needed the revised safeguards: a low-intent 18+ month browser, a represented out-of-area buyer seeking an underwriting answer, and a buyer asking for subjective neighborhood-safety guidance need nurture, route-out, or an objective-criteria redirect—not a consultation push.

sections.heading: the revised *diagnostic contract*
sections.kicker: BUILD THIS NEXT — NOT THE FULL ASSET YET
sections.dek: Preserve 6-3-2 as the strategy while making the buyer experience accurate, useful, and low-burden.

items.why: Use four opening choices: coordinating with another buyer; buying on my own; organizing nonstandard income; or not sure.
A #6-primary, #2-secondary buyer receives the coordination result while Jen sees the income-documentation context.

items.action: Use five structured taps and one optional sentence
items.why: Primary blocker, optional secondary blocker, SFV/commute anchor, timeline, and stage; then 'What feels hardest right now?' Do not repeat these questions in DM.
Each route names one next decision. After delivery, ask whether the buyer wants Jen's help.

items.action: Check representation and consent after the result
items.why: Before offering services, ask whether the buyer is already working under a buyer-representation agreement and whether follow-up is welcome.
Active conversation, nurture fit, and route out. These are service-routing states, not demographic or financial scores.

items.action: Keep financial and legal detail out of Instagram
items.why: No exact income, credit score, tax returns, bank records, Social Security numbers, another buyer's private details, eligibility predictions, or legal conclusions.

rows.claim: #6 — two first-time buyers moved from rate fear to an accepted first offer below list.
rows.evidence: Media 2923821348360719921. The buyers saved for a year, worried about 5–6% rates, and Jen connected them with a lender, helped ease the concern, found a home within weeks, and participated in an offer accepted below list. This proves co-buyer readiness and Jen's coordination, not dual income, two borrowers, or relationship disagreement.

rows.claim: #3 — a singular first-time buyer was guided through a frightening pandemic purchase.
rows.evidence: Media 2322295603977088389. The caption says the team helped her from beginning to end and describes a smooth, successful close. It does not prove that she bought alone, what Jen personally handled, or SFV relevance; the source indicates Palmdale. Jen must confirm those facts before this becomes a Solo Decision Support story.

rows.claim: #2 — Jen has lived empathy, but no archived creative-income buyer case.
rows.evidence: Media 2381170337418068334 documents Jen's family-business background, non-9-to-5 life, operating without steady income, and simultaneous real-estate and clothing work. Across 2,779 captions, the proof pass found no self-employed, freelance, 1099, variable-income, or mortgage-documentation client case. This supports empathy only—not underwriting expertise or a client outcome.

plays.title: Reconcile the authority order
plays.intent: [VERIFIED] Make First Home Valley + 6-3-2 the explicit current strategy without erasing Jen's broader Valley identity or Listing Launch property proof.
plays.command: Decision patch only; no content production yet.
plays.receipt: No live production route can interpret first-time-buyer framing as forbidden.

plays.title: Close the three proof gaps with Jen
plays.intent: Ask three short memory questions: whether the #6 case used two incomes, whether the #3 client bought alone and what Jen carried, and which real transaction best represents a self-employed or mixed-income buyer.
plays.command: Capture exact facts and permissions; do not draft around unknowns.
plays.receipt: Each selected story has a source ID, Jen-action facts, privacy state, and proof ceiling.

plays.title: Review the private diagnostic prototype
plays.intent: The five-step interaction, four micro-results, representation check, consent choices, and Jen reply protocol are now built locally.
plays.command: Watch five people complete it without explanation before any public link change.
plays.receipt: The deterministic test passes 12/12; human comprehension and commercial conversion remain untested.

plays.title: Pilot 20–30 real conversations
plays.intent: Use a manual path so buyer language and Jen's workload decide what deserves automation.
plays.command: Track source post, primary/secondary route, readiness state, consultation, correction, and later business outcome.
plays.receipt: A populated attribution record exists; attention and commercial evidence remain separate.

sections.heading: one system, bounded *expert roles*
sections.body:
Mike Sherrard owns the attention-to-conversation path; his decision change is one manual path instead of a collection of tools. Kallaway owns content jobs and buyer-quality attention; his decision change is blocker-based routing with primary and secondary tags. Jun Yuh owns sourced story packets; his decision change is to withhold unsupported #2 client proof and cap #6 and #3 claims. Alyssa Stalker checks the Instagram-native handoff and lead quality; her decision change is value before qualification and a human reply before booking. Jen remains the voice, privacy, and relationship authority.

The main Jen conductor reconciles these contributions. No additional expert rewrites every asset, and no name counts as proof unless it changed a decision recorded here.

sections.heading: what remains *unconfirmed*
sections.body:
The audit did not open Jen's DMs, submit any calculator, inspect private CRM data, alter Instagram, change Linktree, or publish anything. Saved replies, legacy automations, booking software, CRM ownership, current lender roster, and actual content-sourced consultations remain unconfirmed. Comments and Highlights were excluded at Farrice's direction. The live profile reports 2,780 posts; the proof scan covered 2,779 archived captions, so one live post or caption state is outside this proof pass.

California DRE guidance supports a human-reviewed, privacy-conscious flow and requires buyer-broker agreements as soon as practicable and no later than an offer; Jen and her broker should approve the final operational wording. Fair-housing redirects must use objective, buyer-defined property and commute criteria rather than subjective claims about neighborhood safety or demographics.

Commercial status is UNTESTED. Likes, views, comments, taps, polished tools, and archived transaction stories do not establish attributable leads or closings.
